en: to wail; to sob; to cry

examples.en: My mother sobbed uncontrollably when she heard the news.
The audience sobbed in the last scene of the movie.

examples.ko: 그는 슬픈 소식을 듣고 오열하며 전화를 끊었어요.
examples.en: He hung up the phone, sobbing at the sad news.

examples.ko: 주인공이 오열하는 장면이 오래 기억에 남아요.
examples.en: The scene where the main character sobs stays in my memory.
She held her friend and sobbed.

examples.ko: 가족들이 아무 말도 못 하고 오열하고 있었어요.
examples.en: The family couldn't say anything and was sobbing.

explain: '울다'보다 훨씬 격하게, 목이 메어 흐느끼는 느낌이에요. 뉴스나 소설에서 많이 나오고, 일상에서는 '펑펑 울다'처럼 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: He told the whole story, sobbing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 울면서 다른 행동을 할 때 연결형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Connective form for doing something while sobbing.

phrases.en: Seeing her sobbing made my heart ache.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 형태로, 뉴스에서도 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifier form placed before a noun, often seen in news reports.

phrases.en: I cried my eyes out watching a sad movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '오열하다' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday alternative to the headword.

explain_en: It feels much more intense than '울다', like sobbing with a choked voice. It appears in news and novels, while in daily talk people often say '펑펑 울다'.

examples.ko: 엄마 얼굴을 보자마자 눈물이 왈칵 쏟아졌어요.
examples.en: The moment I saw my mom's face, tears suddenly poured out.

examples.ko: 옛 사진을 보니 그리움이 왈칵 밀려왔어요.
examples.en: Looking at the old photo, a rush of longing came over me.
Someone flung the door open and came in.
While reading the letter, I suddenly burst into tears.
Anger suddenly surged up in me.
The child suddenly burst out crying.

explain: '울컥'은 속에서 치밀어 올라 목이 메는 느낌이고, '왈칵'은 눈물이나 감정이 한꺼번에 쏟아지는 느낌이에요. '눈물이 왈칵 쏟아지다/나다', '왈칵 울다'처럼 써요. 문을 갑자기 세게 열 때도 '왈칵 열다'라고 해요. '와락'은 껴안거나 달려들 때 써서 서로 달라요.

phrases.en: Tears welled up suddenly while I was reading the letter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 눈물이 한꺼번에 쏟아질 때 가장 많이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for tears suddenly flooding out.

phrases.en: My younger brother flung the door open and came in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문을 갑자기 세게 열 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a door is opened suddenly and forcefully.

phrases.en: I choked up when I heard my friend's words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷하지만 '울컥'은 속에서 치밀어 목이 메는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but 'ulkeok' is the feeling of welling up and choking inside.

explain_en: '울컥' is a feeling welling up that tightens the throat, while '왈칵' is tears or emotions pouring out all at once, as in '눈물이 왈칵 쏟아지다/나다' and '왈칵 울다'. You can also say '왈칵 열다' for flinging a door open. '와락' is used for hugging or lunging, so it is different.

en: to be close to tears; to be on the verge of tears

examples.en: The child saw his mother and got teary.
My friend began her story on the verge of tears.

examples.ko: 목소리가 울먹거려서 무슨 일이 있는지 물어봤어요.
examples.en: Her voice was shaky with tears, so I asked what was wrong.
She said thank you in a voice choked with tears.

examples.ko: 혼나고 나서 울먹거리던 동생이 결국 울었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling, who was close to tears after being scolded, finally cried.
At the awards ceremony, he gave his speech with tears welling up.

explain: 완전히 우는 '울다'가 아니라 울음이 터지기 직전, 목소리나 표정에 울음이 섞인 상태예요. 그래서 '울먹거리는 목소리', '울먹거리며 말하다'처럼 말하는 모습과 자주 같이 나와요. 슬픔뿐 아니라 감동했을 때도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: He apologized, close to tears.
phrases.nuance_ko: '울먹거리다'와 같은 뜻이고 조금 더 짧고 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '울먹거리다' but shorter and more common.
phrases.en_equiv: to be on the verge of tears

phrases.en: She answered the phone in a tearful voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목소리에 울음이 섞여 있을 때 '목소리'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '목소리' when tears are mixed into the voice.

phrases.en: Tears welled up in my eyes as I read the letter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 울음이 터지기 전 눈에 눈물이 고인 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes tears gathering in the eyes before crying.

explain_en: It is not full crying like '울다' but the moment just before tears, when your voice or face is mixed with them. So it often pairs with speaking, as in '울먹거리는 목소리' and '울먹거리며 말하다'. It can come from sadness or from being moved.

examples.en: I got a knot in my shoulder, so I had a massage.

examples.ko: 가슴에 맺힌 응어리 때문에 마음이 편하지 않아요.
examples.en: I'm uneasy because of the resentment stuck in my heart.
Once the long misunderstanding was cleared, the bitterness also disappeared.

examples.ko: 목 뒤에 딱딱한 응어리가 만져져서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: I felt a hard lump at the back of my neck, so I went to the hospital.
Try to talk honestly about the feelings you've been holding in.

examples.ko: 서로 응어리를 풀고 다시 친하게 지내기로 했어요.
examples.en: We settled our bad feelings and decided to be close again.

explain: 몸에서는 근육이 뭉쳐서 딱딱해진 곳을 말하고, 마음에서는 오래 풀리지 않은 서운함이나 원망을 말해요. 마음에 쓸 때는 '응어리지다', '응어리가 남다'처럼 말해요. 풀 때는 '응어리를 풀다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 오늘 만나서 이야기하며 오랜 응어리를 풀었어요.
phrases.en: We met and talked today and cleared up our long-held bad feelings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음속에 오래 쌓인 서운함이나 원망을 대화나 시간으로 풀어 없앤다는 뜻이에요. 몸의 응어리가 아니라 마음에만 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means to dissolve hurt or resentment that built up inside through talking or time. It is used only for feelings, not for body knots.

explain_en: For the body it means a hardened spot where a muscle is tight, and for the heart it means lingering hurt or resentment. For feelings you say '응어리지다' or '응어리가 남다'. To let it go, you say '응어리를 풀다'.

en: guilty conscience; remorse; pangs of conscience

examples.ko: 실수한 뒤로 자책감에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: After my mistake, I couldn't sleep because of self-blame.
I feel guilty for not being able to help my friend.

examples.ko: 그는 오랫동안 큰 자책감을 안고 살아왔어요.
examples.en: He has lived for a long time carrying great guilt.
I didn't even want to eat because of the guilt.
Self-reproach gradually fades with time.

examples.ko: 아이를 크게 혼낸 뒤에 자책감이 밀려왔어요.
examples.en: After scolding my child harshly, a wave of regret came over me.

explain: 자기 잘못이나 부족함을 스스로 탓하는 마음이에요. '죄책감'은 잘못에 대한 죄스러움이고, '자책감'은 자신을 탓하는 데 초점이 있어요. '자책감이 들다, 느끼다, 시달리다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 그는 몇 달 동안 자책감에 시달렸어요.
phrases.en: He was tormented by self-blame for several months.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자책하는 마음이 오래 괴롭힐 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for self-blame that torments someone for a long time.

phrases.en: I got angry at my child and felt guilty about it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들다'보다 내가 그 감정을 느낀다는 점이 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes it clearer than 들다 that I am the one feeling it.

phrases.en: As time passed, I finally got free of the guilt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 가진 자책하는 마음이 사라질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when long-held self-blame finally goes away.

explain_en: It is the feeling of blaming yourself for your faults or shortcomings. '죄책감' is guilt over a wrongdoing, while '자책감' focuses on blaming yourself. Common patterns: '자책감이 들다/느끼다/시달리다'.

examples.ko: 시험 때는 잡념이 자꾸 생겨서 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: During exams stray thoughts keep popping up and I can't concentrate.

examples.ko: 잡념을 없애려고 조용히 숨을 쉬어 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried breathing quietly to clear my mind of stray thoughts.
While running, stray thoughts disappear too.

examples.ko: 잡념 때문에 책을 읽어도 내용이 들어오지 않아요.
examples.en: Because of wandering thoughts, nothing sinks in even when I read.

examples.ko: 잡념이 많은 날에는 일찍 자는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: On days with a lot of wandering thoughts, it's good to sleep early.

examples.ko: 청소를 하면 잡념에서 벗어날 수 있어요.
examples.en: Cleaning can help you get away from idle thoughts.

explain: 지금 하는 일과 상관없이 떠오르는 쓸데없는 생각을 말해요. '잡념이 들다/생기다/많다', '잡념을 버리다/없애다'처럼 써요. 걱정과 달리 꼭 불안한 생각이 아니어도 집중을 방해하는 생각이면 잡념이에요. '잡생각'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I have too many stray thoughts, so I can't sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잡념'과 비슷하지만 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 잡념 but more casual in everyday talk.

phrases.en: I shook off my wandering thoughts while exercising.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓸데없는 생각을 완전히 털어 낸다는 뜻이에요. '버리다'보다 단호한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means shaking off pointless thoughts completely; firmer than '버리다'.

phrases.en: I focused on studying without distractions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 생각 없이 한 가지 일에만 몰두한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means being absorbed in one task with no other thoughts.

explain_en: It means useless thoughts that come up and have nothing to do with what you are doing. It is used as '잡념이 들다/생기다/많다' and '잡념을 버리다/없애다'. Unlike worry, any thought that breaks your focus counts, even if it is not anxious. People also say '잡생각'.

examples.en: Cries of anguish from the families could be heard at the accident site.

examples.ko: 그 시는 시대를 향한 시인의 절규 같아요.
examples.en: That poem feels like the poet's outcry toward the age.
A scream close to a wail echoed through the night sky.

examples.ko: 영화의 마지막 장면에서 주인공의 절규는 오래 기억에 남았어요.
examples.en: The main character's cry in the movie's last scene stayed with me for a long time.

examples.ko: 이 그림은 인간의 불안과 절규를 표현했어요.
examples.en: This painting expresses human anxiety and anguish.

examples.ko: 국민의 절규를 정부는 외면하지 말아야 해요.
examples.en: The government should not turn away from the people's outcry.

explain: 단순한 '비명'이나 '고함'보다 고통과 슬픔이 담긴 간절한 외침이에요. 실제 목소리뿐 아니라 시, 그림, 사회의 호소를 비유할 때도 써요. 뭉크의 그림 '절규'로도 알려져 있어요.

phrases.example: 소식을 듣자 사람들 사이에서 절규가 터져 나왔어요.
phrases.en: When they heard the news, cries of anguish burst out among the people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 참았던 슬픔이나 고통이 갑자기 소리로 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when held-in grief or pain suddenly comes out as sound.
phrases.en_equiv: a cry of anguish bursts out

phrases.en: His words were closer to a cry of anguish than to speech.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말투나 글이 매우 간절하고 고통스럽다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the tone or writing is extremely desperate and pained.
phrases.en_equiv: close to a cry of anguish

phrases.en: I was scared and screamed without realizing it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '비명'은 놀람이나 고통에서 나오는 소리이고, '절규'는 더 깊은 슬픔을 담아요.
phrases.nuance_en: '비명' is a sound from shock or pain, while '절규' carries deeper sorrow.

explain_en: Rather than a plain scream or shout, it is an urgent cry filled with pain and sorrow. It can mean an actual voice, but it is also used figuratively for poems, paintings and social appeals. It is also the Korean title of Munch's painting 'The Scream'.

examples.en: He cried out in anguish, calling his child's name.
People were screaming for help.

examples.ko: 절규하는 모습이 뉴스에 나와서 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: Seeing the person cry out on the news broke my heart.
On stage, the actor cries out in tears.

examples.ko: 억울하다고 절규해도 아무도 들어 주지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even though he cried out that it was unfair, nobody listened.

examples.ko: 그는 가슴을 치며 절규하지 않을 수 없었어요.
examples.en: He couldn't help but cry out, beating his chest.

explain: 일상에서는 '소리치다'나 '울부짖다'를 많이 쓰고, '절규하다'는 아주 큰 슬픔이나 분노 때문에 외칠 때 뉴스나 글에서 주로 써요. 장난으로 소리 지를 때는 어울리지 않아요.

phrases.en: I heard a voice crying out in anguish over the phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 슬픔이나 고통이 담긴 목소리를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a voice filled with grief or pain.
phrases.en_equiv: a voice crying out in anguish

phrases.en: The mother called her child's name and wailed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '절규하다'와 비슷하지만 울면서 크게 외치는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '절규하다' but with a stronger feel of crying loudly.

phrases.en: The people shouted for help.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 가장 흔하게 쓰는 말이고, 슬픔이 꼭 담기지는 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common everyday word, and it doesn't necessarily carry sorrow.

explain_en: In daily talk people say '소리치다' or '울부짖다', while '절규하다' is used mostly in news and writing for crying out from deep grief or anger. It does not fit when you are just shouting playfully.

examples.en: Don't be too anxious while you wait for the results.
The closer the pass announcement gets, the more anxious I become.

examples.ko: 마감이 다가올수록 조바심이 커져서 밥도 제대로 못 먹었어요.
examples.en: As the deadline got closer, my anxiety grew and I couldn't even eat properly.

examples.ko: 조바심 내지 말고 천천히 한 걸음씩 준비하면 돼요.
examples.en: Don't be anxious, just prepare slowly, one step at a time.

examples.ko: 친구는 연락이 없어서 하루 종일 조바심하며 기다렸어요.
examples.en: My friend waited all day on edge because there was no word.

examples.ko: 아이가 늦게 오자 엄마는 조바심을 냈어요.
examples.en: When the child came home late, the mother grew anxious.

explain: 일이 잘못될까 봐 마음을 졸이며 서두르는 느낌이에요. '초조해하다'와 비슷하고, 말할 때는 '조바심을 내다', '조바심이 나다'처럼도 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 시험 결과 때문에 너무 조바심을 내지 마세요.
phrases.en: Please don't be too anxious about the test result.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조바심하다'보다 말할 때 훨씬 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is much more common in everyday speech than the verb 조바심하다.

phrases.example: 약속 시간에 늦을 것 같아서 조바심이 나요.
phrases.en: I think I'll be late for the appointment, so I feel anxious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 마음이 급해지고 불안해지는 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the anxious, hurried feeling rises up in you on its own.

phrases.en: Everyone gets nervous before a presentation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조바심하다'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 서두르는 느낌보다 불안한 마음에 더 초점이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning, but it focuses more on the uneasy feeling than on rushing.

explain_en: It has the feel of worrying and getting hurried inside for fear something will go wrong. It is similar to '초조해하다', and in speech it also appears as '조바심을 내다' or '조바심이 나다'.

examples.en: I feel guilty for making my parents worry.
I felt too guilty to even contact you.

examples.ko: 혼자만 편하게 쉬는 것 같아 죄스럽게 느껴져요.
examples.en: I feel guilty, as if I'm the only one resting comfortably.
You can't imagine how guilty I felt for breaking my promise.
It would be a lie to say I don't feel guilty.

examples.ko: 아무것도 못 도와드려서 죄스럽다는 생각이 들었어요.
examples.en: I felt guilty for not being able to help at all.

explain: '미안하다'보다 마음이 무겁고, 특히 부모님이나 어른께 신세를 졌을 때의 송구한 느낌이에요. '죄송하다'가 상대에게 하는 사과 표현이라면 '죄스럽다'는 내 마음의 느낌을 말해요. ㅂ 불규칙이라 '죄스러워요'로 바뀌어요.

phrases.example: 죄스러운 마음에 고개를 들 수 없었어요.
phrases.en: I felt so guilty that I couldn't lift my head.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음의 느낌을 말하는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for describing the feeling.

phrases.en: I felt too guilty to say anything.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 나타내는 '-아서' 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the -아서 connective to give a reason.

phrases.example: 일찍 못 찾아뵌 것을 죄스럽게 생각해요.
phrases.en: I feel guilty that I couldn't visit sooner.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~을/를 죄스럽게 생각하다' 꼴로 어른께 송구한 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the '~을/를 죄스럽게 생각하다' pattern, it expresses a humble sense of guilt toward elders.

explain_en: It feels heavier than '미안하다', a sense of being sorry especially toward parents or elders you owe a lot. While '죄송하다' is an apology you say to someone, '죄스럽다' describes the feeling inside you. It is ㅂ-irregular, becoming '죄스러워요'.

examples.en: After telling a lie, I felt a sense of guilt.

examples.ko: 그는 죄의식 때문에 밤에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: He couldn't sleep at night because of guilt.

examples.ko: 아무 죄의식 없이 쓰레기를 버리는 사람을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw someone throwing away trash without any sense of guilt.

examples.ko: 죄의식을 느끼지 않으려고 일부러 잊으려고 했어요.
examples.en: I tried to forget on purpose so that I wouldn't feel guilty.
I'm tormented by guilt for not having helped my friend.

examples.ko: 죄의식은 시간이 지나도 쉽게 사라지지 않아요.
examples.en: A sense of guilt doesn't easily disappear even as time passes.

explain: '죄책감'과 비슷한데, 죄의식은 '죄의식이 없다'처럼 잘못을 잘못으로 여기는 마음 자체를 말할 때도 써요. '느끼다, 들다, 시달리다'와 자주 같이 나와요.

phrases.en: He didn't feel any sense of guilt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못했다는 마음을 가진다는 뜻으로 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for feeling that you did wrong.

phrases.en: He was tormented by guilt for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미안한 마음 때문에 오래 괴롭다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means suffering for a long time because of a guilty conscience.

phrases.en: Many people feel no guilt even after doing wrong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못을 잘못으로 여기지 않는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes not regarding a wrong as wrong.
phrases.en_equiv: to have no sense of guilt

explain_en: It is close to '죄책감', but 죄의식 can also refer to the very awareness that something is wrong, as in '죄의식이 없다'. It often pairs with '느끼다', '들다' and '시달리다'.

en: to be wretched; to be dismal

examples.en: The scene of the accident is so terrible.
I saw horrific scenes of war on the news.

examples.ko: 참혹하고 슬픈 이야기라 끝까지 읽기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: It was such a harrowing, sad story that it was hard to read to the end.
The damage was far more dreadful than I had thought.

examples.ko: 지진이 지나간 마을은 참혹하게 변해 있었어요.
examples.en: The village hit by the earthquake had been left in a dreadful state.

examples.ko: 참혹한 현실을 외면하면 안 된다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think we should not turn away from the harsh reality.

explain: '끔찍하다'와 비슷하지만 더 무겁고 글에서 많이 써요. 사고, 전쟁, 재난처럼 결과가 너무 비참할 때 '참혹한 모습/현실/광경'으로 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: The village after the flood was a dreadful sight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재난이나 사고 뒤의 비참한 장면을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for the wretched scene after a disaster or accident.

phrases.en: Looking at the war photos, it was truly dreadful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거에 본 비참한 일을 해요체 과거형으로 말하는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite past form for describing a wretched thing you saw.

phrases.en: The news of that accident is so terrible.
phrases.nuance_ko: '참혹하다'보다 일상에서 더 쉽게 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word that is easier to use in daily life than 참혹하다.

explain_en: It is similar to '끔찍하다' (awful) but heavier and more common in writing. It is used when the result of an accident, war or disaster is truly miserable, as in '참혹한 모습/현실/광경'.

examples.en: My friend poured out how hard things were.
The employees voice their complaints to the company.
He shed tears as he spoke of his difficulties.
After I opened up about how I really felt, I felt at ease.
I'm wondering whether to share my worries with my mother.
It's the time when students open up to the teacher about their concerns.

explain: 힘들거나 억울한 마음을 숨기지 않고 털어놓을 때 써요. 보통 '어려움', '불만', '고충' 같은 말과 함께 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '털어놓다'가 더 편하고, '토로하다'는 글이나 뉴스에서 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I told my friend all of my worries.
phrases.nuance_ko: '토로하다'와 뜻이 같고, 일상 대화에서는 이 말이 더 편하고 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 토로하다, but this is the more natural, casual word in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: The customers voiced their complaints about the service.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 글에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말로, 참았던 불만을 겉으로 말한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in news and writing; it means openly voicing a complaint you had held back.

phrases.example: 그는 힘든 마음을 아무에게도 토로하지 못했어요.
phrases.en: He couldn't share his hard feelings with anyone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음을 털어놓고 싶은데 말하지 못하는 상황을 나타낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone wants to share their feelings but cannot bring themselves to say them.
phrases.en_equiv: to be unable to speak out

explain_en: Used when you openly let out hard or unfair feelings. It usually goes with words like 어려움, 불만, and 고충. In casual talk 털어놓다 is more comfortable, while 토로하다 shows up more in writing and the news.

examples.ko: 소식을 듣고 어머니는 바닥에 앉아 통곡하셨어요.
examples.en: After hearing the news, my mother sat on the floor and wailed.

examples.ko: 아이처럼 목놓아 통곡하는 모습을 보니 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: It broke my heart to see him wailing out loud like a child.
The family wept bitterly for a long time in front of the memorial portrait.

examples.ko: 너무 슬퍼서 통곡해도 마음이 풀리지 않았어요.
examples.en: I was so sad that even wailing didn't ease my heart.

examples.ko: 그는 혼자 방에서 통곡하다가 잠이 들었어요.
examples.en: He wept bitterly alone in his room and fell asleep.
Don't wail, just calm down for now.

explain: '울다'보다 훨씬 크고 깊은 슬픔으로 소리 내어 울 때 써요. 조용히 훌쩍이는 '흐느끼다'와 달리 크게 우는 느낌이에요. '통곡을 하다'처럼 명사로도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: At the funeral, all the family members wailed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '통곡하다'를 명사 '통곡'과 '하다'로 나눠 쓴 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same verb split into the noun 통곡 plus 하다.

phrases.en: I heard the sound of wailing from inside the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 우는 소리를 가리킬 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for the sound of loud, grief-filled crying.

phrases.example: 소식을 듣고 아이를 잃은 부모가 대성통곡했어요.
phrases.en: Hearing the news, the parents who lost their child wailed loudly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '통곡하다'보다 더 크게 소리 높여 우는 모습을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Emphasizes crying even more loudly and openly than 통곡하다.

explain_en: It is used for crying out loud from much deeper grief than plain '울다'. Unlike '흐느끼다', which is quiet sobbing, it feels like loud wailing. The noun form is also common, as in '통곡을 하다'.

examples.en: My little brother grumbles that he doesn't want to clean.
He grumbled every morning about getting up early.
Stop grumbling and help me a bit.
Father grumbled, but in the end he drove me there.
My friend was grumbling something to himself.

examples.ko: 툴툴거리지 말고 하고 싶은 말을 해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't mutter; say what you want to say.

explain: '투덜거리다'와 비슷하지만 목소리를 낮게 깔고 퉁명스럽게 불평하는 느낌이 강해요. 보통 '~다고 툴툴거리다'처럼 쓰고, 불평하면서도 결국 할 일은 하는 사람에게 자주 써요. 큰 소리로 따지는 '항의하다'와는 달라요.

phrases.en: My older brother keeps grumbling that he has a lot of homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: '툴툴거리다'와 뜻이 거의 같고 말하기에 조금 더 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means almost the same as '툴툴거리다' and is a bit easier to say.

phrases.en: My younger sibling grumbled but still did the dishes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불평하면서 어떤 일을 하는 모습을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for someone who complains while doing a task.

phrases.en: The child is complaining that it's raining.
phrases.nuance_ko: '툴툴거리다'보다 일반적이에요. 퉁명스러운 느낌은 조금 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: More general than '툴툴거리다', with a weaker sense of curtness.

explain_en: It is similar to '투덜거리다' but has a stronger feel of grumbling bluntly in a low voice. It is usually used like '~다고 툴툴거리다', often for someone who complains but ends up doing the job anyway. It differs from '항의하다', which is protesting loudly.

examples.en: He lamented his situation.
Lamenting won't change anything.
Grandfather sighs in dismay when he looks at young people these days.
Don't keep lamenting just because you failed the exam.

examples.ko: 물가가 오르는 것을 한탄하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people bemoan rising prices.
There's no use lamenting; it's already in the past.

explain: 어쩔 수 없는 일 때문에 한숨을 쉬며 슬퍼하거나 탓하는 모습에 써요. '불평하다'와 달리 상대에게 요구하기보다 혼자 안타까워하는 느낌이에요. '신세를 한탄하다', '처지를 한탄하다'처럼 '신세', '처지'와 잘 어울려요.

phrases.example: 그는 자기 신세를 한탄하며 한숨을 쉬었어요.
phrases.en: He lamented his own lot and sighed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '한탄하다'와 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common partner phrase of 한탄하다.

phrases.en: Don't just lament; let's look for a way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 슬퍼하기만 하고 아무것도 하지 않을 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone only grieves and does nothing.

phrases.example: 어쩔 수 없다며 그는 한숨을 쉬었어요.
phrases.en: Saying there was nothing he could do, he sighed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '한탄하다'보다 쉽고, 말보다 행동으로 안타까움을 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 한탄하다; shows regret through action rather than words.

explain_en: Used for sighing and grieving or blaming over something that can't be helped. Unlike 불평하다, it feels like regretting alone rather than making demands of someone. It goes well with 신세 and 처지, as in 신세를 한탄하다 and 처지를 한탄하다.

examples.ko: 열심히 준비한 발표가 취소돼 허탈감이 컸어요.
examples.en: The presentation I prepared so hard was canceled, and I felt very deflated.
After passing, I actually felt let down.

examples.ko: 경기에서 져서 팀 전체가 허탈감에 빠졌어요.
examples.en: The whole team sank into dejection after losing the game.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝나고 나니 허탈감 때문에 아무것도 하기 싫어요.
examples.en: Now the exam is over, I feel drained and do not want to do anything.

examples.ko: 큰 프로젝트를 마친 뒤의 허탈감을 어떻게 이겨 내요?
examples.en: How do you overcome the letdown after finishing a big project?

examples.ko: 허탈감이 밀려와서 한참 멍하니 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: A wave of deflation hit me, and I sat there in a daze for a while.

explain: 기대했던 일이 끝나거나 어긋난 뒤에 몸과 마음에서 힘이 쭉 빠지는 느낌이에요. '허무감'이 모든 게 덧없다는 느낌이라면, 허탈감은 어떤 일을 겪은 뒤의 맥 빠진 기분에 더 가까워요.

phrases.en: After losing the game, I felt dejected.
phrases.nuance_ko: '느끼다'보다 감정이 저절로 마음에 찾아오는 느낌으로, 일이 끝난 직후의 기분을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Compared with 'to feel', it sounds like the emotion arrives on its own, often right after something ends.

phrases.example: 큰 시험이 끝나고 한동안 허탈감에 빠졌어요.
phrases.en: After the big exam ended, I fell into a slump for a while.
phrases.nuance_ko: 허탈한 기분이 꽤 오래 이어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the deflated feeling lasts for some time.

phrases.en: I feel so empty after hearing the result.
phrases.nuance_ko: 허탈감을 형용사로 말한 것이라서 일상 대화에서 '허탈감이 들다'보다 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the adjective form, and it is more common in everyday speech than the noun phrase.

explain_en: It is the feeling of strength draining out after something you expected ends or goes wrong. While '허무감' is a sense that everything is fleeting, 허탈감 is closer to the deflated mood after a specific event.

en: venting anger; taking it out on someone

examples.en: Please do not take it out on others for no reason.
Some people vent their anger by cleaning.
That is not a conversation, it is just venting.
My friend sang loudly to blow off steam.

examples.ko: 어디에도 화풀이할 곳이 없어서 밖을 걸었어요.
examples.en: I had nowhere to vent my anger, so I walked outside.
If you need someone to vent to, tell me.

explain: 화가 난 마음을 터뜨리는 일인데, 화나게 한 사람이 아닌 다른 사람이나 물건에 풀 때 많이 써서 부정적이에요. '화풀이를 하다', '화풀이 상대'처럼 써요. 비슷한 말로 '분풀이'가 있어요.

phrases.example: 저는 동생의 화풀이 상대가 되기 싫어요.
phrases.en: I don't want to be my younger sibling's target for venting anger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화를 쏟아내는 대상을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person who receives the anger.

phrases.en: You shouldn't throw things to vent your anger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻이고 둘 다 부정적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning; both sound negative.

phrases.en: You shouldn't take your anger out on your younger sibling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '을/를 하다'를 붙여 화를 터뜨리는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 을/를 하다 describes the act of venting anger.

explain_en: It is the act of letting out anger, usually on someone or something other than the cause, so it sounds negative. Use '화풀이를 하다' and '화풀이 상대'. A similar word is '분풀이'.

examples.ko: 정치에 환멸을 느껴서 뉴스를 안 봐요.
examples.en: I'm disillusioned with politics, so I don't watch the news.
After long expectations, only disillusionment was left.

examples.ko: 직장 생활에 환멸이 와서 쉬고 싶어요.
examples.en: I've become disenchanted with work life and want to take a break.
I quit that job because of my disillusionment.
The gap between ideal and reality led to disillusionment.
As my disillusionment deepened, my motivation vanished too.

explain: '실망'보다 강해서, 믿고 기대했던 사람, 제도, 일에 정이 떨어질 만큼 실망했을 때 써요. '환멸을 느끼다'가 가장 기본이 되는 짝이에요. '환멸감'이라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 그 일 이후로 친구에게 환멸감이 들었어요.
phrases.en: After that incident, I felt disillusioned with my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '환멸'과 같은 뜻으로, 느낌을 강조하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 환멸, stressing the feeling.

phrases.en: I became disillusioned with people.
phrases.nuance_ko: '환멸을 느끼다'와 비슷하게 마음에 환멸이 생길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 환멸을 느끼다, used when disillusionment arises in one's mind.

phrases.en: I was very disappointed with the result.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환멸보다 약한 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier expression that is weaker than 환멸.

explain_en: It is stronger than '실망' and is used when you were so let down by a person, system or job you trusted that you lose all affection for it. '환멸을 느끼다' is the most basic pairing. It can also be said as '환멸감'.

en: filial devotion; devotion to one's parents

examples.en: That son is deeply devoted to his parents.
A devoted daughter takes care of her parents.
Grandmother was moved by her grandson's devotion.
He is known for his devotion to his parents.

examples.ko: 효성은 말이 아니라 행동으로 보여 줘야 해요.
examples.en: Filial devotion should be shown by actions, not words.

examples.ko: 옛날이야기에는 효성이 큰 아이가 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Old tales often feature a child with great filial devotion.

explain: '효도'가 부모님께 하는 행동이라면 '효성'은 부모를 위하는 마음이에요. '효성이 지극하다', '효성이 깊다'처럼 마음의 크기를 말할 때 써요. 말투가 조금 옛날 같아서 요즘은 '효도'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The daughter did her utmost out of devotion to her parents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음을 다해서 부모님을 위한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to give one's whole heart in caring for one's parents.
phrases.en_equiv: to be fully devoted to one's parents

phrases.en: The devoted daughter calls her parents every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부모를 위하는 마음이 큰 사람이나 행동을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a person or action that shows great care for parents.

phrases.en: He is well known in the neighborhood as a dutiful son.
phrases.nuance_ko: 효성이 깊은 아들을 말하고, 딸은 '효녀'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A son who is devoted to his parents; for a daughter, say '효녀'.

explain_en: If 효도 is what you do for your parents, 효성 is the heart behind it. It is used to describe how strong that feeling is, as in 효성이 지극하다 or 효성이 깊다. It sounds a little old-fashioned, so people today use 효도 more.

examples.ko: 아이는 엄마를 보자 흑흑 울기 시작했어요.
examples.en: The child started sobbing as soon as she saw her mother.

examples.ko: 방에서 누가 흑흑 소리 내며 울고 있어요.
examples.en: Someone in the room is crying with sobs.
My friend sobbed, saying she failed the exam.
Sob, sob, my beloved puppy is gone!

examples.ko: 드라마를 보다가 나도 모르게 흑흑 울었어요.
examples.en: While watching a drama, I found myself sobbing.

examples.ko: 그는 한참을 흑흑 흐느끼다가 겨우 말을 꺼냈어요.
examples.en: He sobbed for a long while before he could finally speak.

explain: 우는 소리를 흉내 낸 말이에요. 크게 우는 '엉엉'과 달리 숨을 삼키듯 작게 우는 느낌이고, 채팅에서는 슬픈 척 장난스럽게 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: I cried and sobbed while watching the movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: '울다' 앞에 붙여 작게 숨을 삼키며 우는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before 'cry' to describe crying quietly with caught breath.

phrases.example: 아이가 흑흑 소리를 내며 방에 들어갔어요.
phrases.en: The child went into the room making sobbing sounds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우는 소리를 직접 흉내 내어 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression that directly imitates the sound of crying.

phrases.example: 채팅에서 친구가 '숙제가 너무 많아요, 슬퍼요 흑흑'이라고 썼어요.
phrases.en: In the chat, my friend wrote, 'There's so much homework, I'm sad, boohoo.'
phrases.nuance_ko: 채팅에서 슬픈 척 장난스럽게 문장 끝에 덧붙이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A playful add-on at the end of a sentence in chats, pretending to be sad.

explain_en: It imitates the sound of crying. Unlike '엉엉', which is loud crying, it feels like quiet sobbing with held breath, and in chats people also use it jokingly to act sad.
